transliteration_key.2: ء، وكذلك ق كما ينطقها اللبنانيون (مثل 2ahwe = قهوة)

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: صباح الخير كريم، كيفك؟
dialogue.english: Good morning Karim, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: صباح النور ريما، منيح، بس لسّا نعسان.
dialogue.transliteration: sabaa7 en-nuur Riima, mniih, bas lissa na3saan.
dialogue.english: Good morning Rima, good, but I'm still sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: أنا فقت بكير اليوم. قديش الساعة هلأ؟
dialogue.transliteration: ana fe2t bakkiir el-yom. 2addeesh es-saa3a halla2?
dialogue.english: I woke up early today. What time is it now?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: الساعة سبعة.
dialogue.english: It's seven o'clock.

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: بدّي قهوة أول شي. الدني برد كتير الصبح بكير.
dialogue.transliteration: baddi 2ahwe awwal shi. ed-denye bard ktiir eS-Sob7 bakkiir.
dialogue.english: I want coffee first thing. Early morning is very cold.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: وأنا غسلت وجّي ونضّفت سنّاني، بس لسّا نعسان.
dialogue.transliteration: w ana ghasalt wijji w naDDaft snaani, bas lissa na3saan.
dialogue.english: And I washed my face and brushed my teeth, but I'm still sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: لبست تيابك؟ لازم نطلع.
dialogue.english: Did you get dressed? We have to go.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: إي، لبست تيابي. بس فاتني الباص مبارح.
dialogue.transliteration: ee, lbist tyaabi. bas faatni el-baaS mbaare7.
dialogue.english: Yes, I got dressed. But I missed the bus yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: ما تخاف، رح آخدك بالسيارة.
dialogue.english: Don't worry, I'll take you in the car.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: يسلمو إيديكي ريما.
dialogue.english: Bless your hands, Rima (thank you).

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمّك، يلّا نطلع.
dialogue.english: Don't mention it, let's go.

lessons.culture: A Lebanese morning greeting is "صباح الخير" answered with "صباح النور", or the warmer "صباح الورد". A small cup of coffee at home before leaving is close to universal, and Beirut morning traffic is heavy enough that people leave early.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "صباح الخير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.feedback: This is a wordy, ceremonial reply; in ordinary speech it is just صباح النور.

exercises.tip: "صباح النور" always answers "صباح الخير"; "صباح الورد" is the warmer alternative.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "قديش الساعة هلأ؟" Answer that it's seven o'clock.

too_formal.feedback: This is how a newsreader states the time, not how it is said in a conversation.

exercises.tip: Say "الساعة" and the number; no ordinal is needed.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "بدّي _____ أول شي." English meaning: I want coffee first thing.

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic, but it drops the everyday بدّي.

exercises.tip: In Lebanese ق is usually a glottal stop, so قهوة sounds like 2ahwe.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "الدني _____ كتير الصبح بكير." English meaning: Early morning is very cold.

too_formal.item: الجو بارد جداً في الصباح الباكر
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but it is written style; the spoken sentence is short and uses الدني for the weather.

exercises.tip: "الدني برد" is the natural way to say it is cold out.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Lebanese Arabic: "I woke up early."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: "بكير" is the everyday word for early.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I missed the bus."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but الحافلة is the bookish word; people say الباص.

exercises.tip: "فاتني" is the verb for missing a bus or a chance.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'm still sleepy."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but ما زلت is written style; spoken Lebanese uses لسّا.

exercises.tip: Use نعسانة when a woman says it about herself.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I left for work"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but غادرت إلى is written style.

exercises.tip: "طلع" means leave a place, and عالشغل means to work.

exercises.prompt: Which reply fits "صباح الخير" best?

too_formal.feedback: Too wordy; the short reply is what people say.

exercises.tip: The reply mirrors the greeting with النور.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "بكير / عالشغل / طلعت"

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: The verb comes first, then where, then when.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: وصلت عالشغل أخيراً، كان في زحمة كتير.
dialogue.transliteration: wSelt 3ash-shghol akhiiran, kaan fii za7me ktiir.
dialogue.english: I finally arrived at work, there was a lot of traffic.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: عندي اجتماع الساعة عشرة، ولازم خلّص هالشغلة قبل الضهر.
dialogue.transliteration: 3indi ijtimaa3 es-saa3a 3ashra, w laazem khallis hash-shaghle 2abl eD-Dohor.
dialogue.english: I have a meeting at ten, and I have to finish this task before noon.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: شو الأخبار اليوم؟ عندك شغل كتير؟
dialogue.english: What's the news today? Do you have a lot of work?

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: إي، عندي شغل كتير هلأ، وعم فتّش على قلمي من الصبح.
dialogue.transliteration: ee, 3indi shghol ktiir halla2, w 3am fattesh 3ala 2alami men eS-Sob7.
dialogue.english: Yes, I have a lot of work now, and I've been looking for my pen since morning.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: هيدا قلمك عالطاولة!
dialogue.english: That's your pen on the table!

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: يسلمو إيديك! وأنا جوعانة، بدّي آكل شي.
dialogue.transliteration: yislamu iideek! w ana joo3aane, baddi aakol shi.
dialogue.english: Bless your hands! And I'm hungry, I want to eat something.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: وين بتتغدّي؟
dialogue.english: Where do you have lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: بالبيت بالعادة، بس اليوم بتغدّى هون.
dialogue.transliteration: bil-beet bil-3aade, bas el-yom batghadda hon.
dialogue.english: At home usually, but today I'm having lunch here.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: أنا تعبان شوي هلأ. فيّي آخد استراحة؟
dialogue.transliteration: ana ta3baan shwayy halla2. fiyyi aakhod isteraa7a?
dialogue.english: I'm a bit tired now. Can I take a break?

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: أكيد، تفضّل.
dialogue.english: Sure, go ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: يسلمو، رح إتصل فيك بعد الضهر.
dialogue.transliteration: yislamu, ra7 ettaSel fiik ba3d eD-Dohor.
dialogue.english: Thanks, I'll call you in the afternoon.

lessons.culture: In Lebanon lunch is often the biggest meal of the day, and many people still eat it at home or with colleagues in the early afternoon. "شو الأخبار؟" is a routine greeting between colleagues, and the usual answer is "الحمدلله" rather than real news.

exercises.prompt: A coworker asks: "وين بتتغدّى؟" Reply that you eat at home.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: The short answer is just the place, with بـ.

exercises.prompt: A coworker asks: "فيّي آخد استراحة؟" Say yes, go ahead.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds stiff and official.

exercises.tip: "تفضّل" invites someone to go ahead; say تفضّلي to a woman.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "عندي اجتماع الساعة _____." English meaning: I have a meeting at ten.

too_formal.feedback: This is the written ordinal; speech uses the plain number after الساعة.

exercises.tip: Numbers after الساعة are plain: سبعة, عشرة.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "_____، بدّي آكل شي." English meaning: I'm hungry, I want to eat something.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but جائع is the written word; people say جوعان.

exercises.tip: A woman says جوعانة.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Lebanese Arabic: "I have a lot of work now."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: "عندي" says "I have", and كتير means a lot.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll call you in the afternoon."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: "رح" makes the future; فيك is "you" (فيكي to a woman).

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I finished my work early today."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: "خلّص" is the everyday word for finish.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I'm a bit tired now"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: "شوي" softens the word: a bit.

exercises.prompt: Which word completes: "عم فتّش على _____." English meaning: I'm looking for my pen.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: "عم" before a verb means it is happening now.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "بكير / وصلت / عالشغل"

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: Same order as before: verb, place, time.

reply.english: And you (too), lit. you are of its people.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: مسا الخير ريما، رجعت عالبيت؟
dialogue.english: Good evening Rima, did you come back home?

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: مسا النور، إي رجعت. تعبت كتير اليوم.
dialogue.transliteration: masa en-nuur, ee rje3t. ti3ibt ktiir el-yom.
dialogue.english: Good evening, yes I came back. I got very tired today.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: وأنا بدّي إتحمّم أول شي. وبعدين شو رح نتعشّى؟
dialogue.transliteration: w ana baddi et7ammam awwal shi. w ba3deen shu ra7 net3ashsha?
dialogue.english: And I want to shower first. Then what will we have for dinner?

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: ما بعرف، شو بدّك؟
dialogue.english: I don't know, what do you want?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: منطلب شي؟
dialogue.english: Shall we order something?

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: تمام. وبعدين بدنا نتفرّج ع مسلسل؟
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam. w ba3deen biddna netfarraj 3a musalsal?
dialogue.english: Fine. And then do we want to watch a series?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: يلّا، بس أول خلّينا نطلع نتمشّى شوي، الجو حلو بالمسا.
dialogue.transliteration: yalla, bas awwal khallina neTla3 netmashsha shwayy, el-jaww 7ilu bil-masa.
dialogue.english: Yes, but first let's go out for a little walk, the weather is nice in the evening.

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: فكرة حلوة، بس بدّي إتّصل بأهلي أول شي.
dialogue.transliteration: fikra 7ilwe, bas baddi ettaSel b-ahli awwal shi.
dialogue.english: Nice idea, but I want to call my family first.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: تمام. أنا رح نام بكير الليلة.
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam. ana ra7 naam bakkiir el-leele.
dialogue.english: Fine. I'll sleep early tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: تصبح على خير.
dialogue.english: Good night.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: وإنتي من أهله.
dialogue.english: And you (too).

pair.english: What will we have for dinner?

lessons.culture: "تصبح على خير" is answered with the fixed phrase "وإنت من أهله" (literally: you are of its people), so it is learned whole rather than word by word. Lebanese evenings start late, with dinner often at eight or nine and a walk or a coffee with friends before or after.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "مسا الخير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but the long form sounds ceremonial; the short one is everyday.

exercises.tip: "مسا النور" mirrors the greeting, like the morning pair.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "تصبح على خير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.feedback: Understandable, but people answer with the fixed phrase.

exercises.tip: Say وإنتي to a woman; the ending أهله stays the same.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "بدّي _____، تعبت كتير اليوم." English meaning: I want to shower, I got very tired today.

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic, but Lebanese speech says إتحمّم for showering.

exercises.tip: "إتحمّم" comes from حمّام, a bath.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "خلّينا نطلع _____ شوي." English meaning: Let's go out for a little walk.

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic, but it is not how a friend would suggest it.

exercises.tip: "خلّينا" plus a verb is the everyday way to say let's.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Lebanese Arabic: "I came back home."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: "رجعت" is said rje3t in Lebanese.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll sleep early tonight."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: "رح" plus the plain verb makes the future.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The weather is nice in the evening."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: "حلو" is the everyday word for nice.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Good night"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like a translation, not the phrase people use.

exercises.tip: Say تصبحي على خير to a woman.

exercises.prompt: Which reply fits "كيف كان يومك؟" best?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: "بس" means but.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "عالبيت / رجعت / بكير"

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: Verb, place, then time.

phrases.arabic: الْأُسْبُوع الْجَاي فِي اجْتِمَاع يَوم التِّلَاتَا
phrases.transliteration: el-esbuu3 el-jeyy fii ijtimaa3 yom et-tlaate

phrases.arabic: كِل يَوم عِنْدي شُغِل غَيِر الْجُمْعَة وَالسَّبِت
phrases.transliteration: kell yom 3indi shghol gheer ej-jum3a wes-sabt

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: بعدني ما قررت، ليش، عندك فكرة؟
dialogue.english: I haven't decided yet, why, do you have an idea?

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: السبت منروح عالسوق، بدّك تجي؟
dialogue.english: On Saturday we're going to the market, do you want to come?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: أكيد. بس اليوم شو يوم؟ خربطت الأيام.
dialogue.transliteration: akiid. bas el-yom shu yom? kharbaTt el-ayyaam.
dialogue.english: Sure. But what day is today? I've mixed up the days.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: اليوم يوم الأحد، وبكرا يوم التنين.
dialogue.transliteration: el-yom yom el-a7ad, w bukra yom et-tneen.
dialogue.english: Today is Sunday, and tomorrow is Monday.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: والأسبوع الجاي في اجتماع يوم التلاتا.
dialogue.transliteration: w el-esbuu3 el-jeyy fii ijtimaa3 yom et-tlaate.
dialogue.english: And next week there's a meeting on Tuesday.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: إيمتى بالضبط؟
dialogue.english: When exactly?

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: يوم التلاتا الساعة عشرة.
dialogue.english: Tuesday at ten o'clock.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: طيب، الخميس بشوف أصحابي، والجمعة بروح عالجامع.
dialogue.transliteration: Tayyeb, el-khamiis bshuuf aS7aabi, w ej-jum3a broo7 3aj-jaami3.
dialogue.english: Okay, Thursday I see my friends, and Friday I go to the mosque.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: أنا كل يوم عندي شغل غير السبت والأحد.
dialogue.transliteration: ana kell yom 3indi shghol gheer es-sabt wel-a7ad.
dialogue.english: I have work every day except Saturday and Sunday.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: نهاية الأسبوع بتجي بسرعة، الحمدلله.
dialogue.english: The weekend comes quickly, thank God.

pair.english: What do you plan to do on the weekend?

response.english: We're going to the market on Saturday.
No, Saturday is a day off.

lessons.culture: The Lebanese work week usually runs Monday to Friday, with Sunday the common day off and many shops and some offices open on Saturday morning. Friday is the midday prayer day for Muslims and Sunday is church day for Christians; the pattern "except Friday and Saturday" belongs to places with that weekend, in Lebanon people more often say Saturday and Sunday. "إيمتى؟" is the everyday word for when.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "إيمتى الاجتماع؟" Say it's on Tuesday.

too_formal.feedback: This sounds like an official announcement, not a quick spoken answer.

exercises.tip: "يوم" plus the day name is the everyday answer to when.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "اليوم شو يوم؟" Say today is Sunday.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatical, but the linking word هو makes it sound written.

exercises.tip: "اليوم يوم" plus the day needs no linking word.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "بكرا يوم _____." English meaning: Tomorrow is Monday.

too_formal.feedback: This is the written spelling; Lebanese say التنين.

exercises.tip: "التنين" is Monday out loud in Lebanon.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "السبت _____ عالسوق." English meaning: On Saturday we go to the market.

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic, but it is not how people speak.

exercises.tip: "منروح" is the we form of go in Lebanese.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Lebanese Arabic: "Friday is the day of prayer and rest."

too_formal.item: يوم الجمعة هو يوم للصلاة والراحة
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but the extra linking words sound written.

exercises.tip: "الجمعة يوم" plus the thing needs no linking word.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I have work every day except Friday and Saturday."

accepted: كِل يَوم عِنْدي شُغِل غَيِر الْجُمْعَة وَالسَّبِت
kell yom 3indi shghol gheer ej-jum3a wes-sabt
كل يوم عندي شغل إلا الجمعة والسبت
عندي شغل كل يوم غير الجمعة والسبت
kell yom 3indi shghol illa ej-jum3a wes-sabt

too_formal.item: لدي عمل كل يوم باستثناء الجمعة والسبت
too_formal.feedback: Correct, but written style; غير or إلا is the spoken word for except.

exercises.tip: "غير" before the days left out means except.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The weekend comes quickly."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but it sounds like writing or a news reader, not something said out loud.

exercises.tip: "بتجي" is she comes, and نهاية is a feminine word.

exercises.prompt: Which word means "Thursday"?

too_formal.feedback: Adding a description is unnecessary for just naming a day.

exercises.tip: "الخميس" alone already means Thursday.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "What do you plan to do on the weekend?"

too_formal.item: ماذا تنوي أن تفعل في عطلة نهاية الأسبوع؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but the extra linking word أن makes it sound written.

exercises.tip: "ناوي" straight before the verb states an intention (ناوية for a woman).

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "الأحد / يوم / اليوم"

too_formal.feedback: Grammatical, but the linking word هو is dropped in speech.

exercises.tip: "اليوم يوم" plus the day name needs nothing extra.

phrases.english: I'm learning to write Arabic calligraphy.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: كتير منيح! أنا ما بحبّ القراية كتير.
dialogue.transliteration: ktiir mniih! ana ma b7ebb el-2raaye ktiir.
dialogue.english: Very good! I don't like reading much.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: صحتين! شو طبخت؟
dialogue.english: Bon appétit! What did you cook?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: مجدّرة وفتّوش.
dialogue.english: Mujaddara and fattoush.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: ويوم الأحد بطلع عالجبل مع رفقاتي.
dialogue.transliteration: w yom el-a7ad beTla3 3al-jabal ma3 rfe2aati.
dialogue.english: And on Sunday I go up the mountain with my friends.

pair.english: What do you do in your free time?
Do you have time this evening?

response.english: No, today I'm at my parents'.

lessons.culture: Weekend hikes in the mountains above Beirut and long Sunday lunches with the family are favourite ways to spend free time, and Arabic calligraphy classes are popular in cultural centres. In Lebanese "jem3a" means both Friday and a whole week, so "kell jem3a" is "every week".

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "شو بتعمل بوقت فراغك؟" Say you read and cook.

too_formal.feedback: Written verbs. Speech adds b-: be2ra, beTbokh.

exercises.tip: The b- in front of a verb marks the everyday present.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "عندك وقت اليوم المسا؟" Say yes, after the sunset prayer.

too_formal.feedback: na3am is written Arabic. Speech says ee (or eh).

exercises.tip: el-maghreb names both the sunset prayer and that time of day.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "بقرا كتاب كلّ _____." Meaning: I read a book every week.

too_formal.feedback: osbuu3iyyan is written Arabic. Speech says kell jem3a.

exercises.tip: jem3a means both Friday and week.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "بزرع ورد بال_____." Meaning: I grow flowers in the garden.

too_formal.feedback: 7adii2a is understood, but a home garden is a jneene.

exercises.tip: ward means flowers (and roses).

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I like cooking."

too_formal.feedback: Without b- it sounds written. Speech says b7ebb.

exercises.tip: b7ebb = I like/love.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Do you like Arabic calligraphy?" (to a man)

too_formal.feedback: hal is written Arabic. Speech asks with the voice.

exercises.tip: To a woman: bt7ebbi el-khaTT el-3arabi?

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I spend my time with my family."

too_formal.feedback: usra is written Arabic. Speech says 3iilti.

exercises.tip: 2aDDa = to spend (time).

exercises.prompt: Which word means "hobby"?
exercises.tip: 2raaye is reading, sbaa7a is swimming, khaTT is calligraphy.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Time passes quickly when I read"?
exercises.tip: byemro2 (it passes) is a very Levantine verb.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "عالجبال / بطلع / رفقاتي / مع".

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic. Speech says beTla3 3al-jbaal.

exercises.tip: Tele3 3al-jabal is the everyday way to say you go up into the mountains.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "العشا / مبارح / لعيلتي / طبخت".

too_formal.feedback: ams and usra are written Arabic. Speech says mbaare7 and 3iilti.

exercises.tip: mbaare7 (yesterday) usually comes first.

dialogue.speaker: Ziad
dialogue.arabic: وبالمسا بلعب فوتبول مع رفقاتي بالملعب.
dialogue.transliteration: w bel-masa bel3ab football ma3 rfe2aati bel-mal3ab.
dialogue.english: And in the evening I play football with my friends at the pitch.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: وأنا كمان! في ماتش اليوم؟
dialogue.transliteration: w ana kamaan! fii match el-yom?
dialogue.english: Me too! Is there a match today?

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: منيح. هلّق أنا رايح عالجيم.
dialogue.english: Good. Right now I'm off to the gym.

dialogue.speaker: Ziad
dialogue.arabic: شو بتعمل بالجيم؟
dialogue.english: What do you do at the gym?

lessons.culture: Football is Lebanon's most followed sport, with Beirut clubs such as Nejmeh and Ansar drawing big crowds, and basketball is a close second. Many people walk or run along the Corniche by the sea early in the morning or after the evening prayer.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "بتعمل رياضة؟" Say yes, every day.

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic. Speech says ee, kell yom.

exercises.tip: kell yom = every day; kell jem3a = every week.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: "منتمشّى سوا بعد الصلا؟" Agree.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but stiff. Speech says yalla, akiid.

exercises.tip: yalla means "come on, let's go".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أيّا فريق _____؟" Meaning: Which team do you support?

too_formal.feedback: Without b- the verb sounds written. Speech says btshajje3.

exercises.tip: To a woman: btshajj3i.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "تعبت، _____ ميّ." Meaning: I'm tired, I need water.

too_formal.feedback: a7taaj is written Arabic. Lebanese use baddi for both want and need.

exercises.tip: baddi = I want / I need.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I run every morning."

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic. Speech says berkoD kell yom eS-Sob7.

exercises.tip: eS-Sob7 = in the morning.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The match starts at eight."

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic. Speech says el-match byballesh es-saa3a tmaane.

exercises.tip: ballash = to start; match is said as in English.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Exercise is good for health."

too_formal.feedback: mufiide is fine but formal. Speech says mnii7a.

exercises.tip: mniih / mnii7a = good.

exercises.prompt: Which word means "bicycle"?

too_formal.feedback: darraaje is understood, but Lebanese say biskliit, from French.

exercises.tip: 7Saan is horse, Taabe is ball, mal3ab is pitch.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I lift weights at the gym"?
exercises.tip: Many people also say berfa3 7diid, "I lift iron".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "فوتبول / بلعب / رفقاتي / مع".

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic. Speech says bel3ab football.

exercises.tip: rfe2aati = my friends.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "حصان / بركب / الجمعة / يوم".

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic. Speech says berkab 7Saan.

exercises.tip: yom ej-jem3a = on Friday.

challenge.title: Plan Your Week in Lebanese
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short conversation about a day and the week ahead, at least 10 lines. It must include a morning greeting and its reply, a question about the time, a statement about being tired or sleepy, an evening greeting and its reply, the good-night exchange, a question about a day of the week or a meeting time, and a plan for the weekend. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 7.
required_elements: A morning greeting using صباح الخير and its reply صباح النور.
A statement about waking up or being sleepy, using فقت بكير or لسّا نعسان.
A question using قديش الساعة؟ and a time answer.
A statement about being tired or having a lot of work, using تعبت or عندي شغل كتير.
An evening greeting using مسا الخير and its reply مسا النور.
The good-night exchange using تصبح على خير and وإنت من أهله.
A question using إيمتى؟ and its answer.
A statement naming at least two days of the week.
A plan for the weekend using نهاية الأسبوع.
At least one invitation or suggestion, such as بدّك تجي؟ or خلّينا نطلع.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: صباح الخير كريم، كيفك اليوم؟
dialogue.english: Good morning Karim, how are you today?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: صباح النور، منيح، بس لسّا نعسان شوي.
dialogue.transliteration: sabaa7 en-nuur, mniih, bas lissa na3saan shwayy.
dialogue.english: Good morning, good, but still a bit sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: قَدِّيش السَّاعَة هَلْأ؟
dialogue.english: What time is it now?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: الساعة سبعة، لازم إطلع عالشغل بسرعة.
dialogue.english: It's seven, I have to leave for work quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: طيب، إيمتى بترجع المسا؟
dialogue.english: Okay, when will you be back in the evening?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: بعد الضهر، عندي شغل كتير هلأ.
dialogue.english: In the afternoon, I have a lot of work now.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: طيب، مسا الخير لما ترجع.
dialogue.english: Okay, good evening when you get back.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: مسا النور، تعبت كتير اليوم بصراحة.
dialogue.transliteration: masa en-nuur, ti3ibt ktiir el-yom bSaraa7a.
dialogue.english: Good evening, I got really tired today, honestly.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: خلّينا نطلع نتمشّى شوي.
dialogue.english: Let's go out for a little walk.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: فكرة حلوة، بس بدّي إتحمّم أول شي.
dialogue.transliteration: fikra 7ilwe, bas baddi et7ammam awwal shi.
dialogue.english: Good idea, but I want to shower first.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: تمام، شو ناوي تعمل بنهاية الأسبوع؟
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, shu naawi ta3mel b-nihaayet el-esbuu3?
dialogue.english: Great, what do you plan to do on the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: السبت منروح عالسوق، والخميس بشوف أصحابي. بدّك تجي؟
dialogue.transliteration: es-sabt mnruu7 3as-suu2, w el-khamiis bshuuf aS7aabi. baddik tiji?
dialogue.english: On Saturday we're going to the market, and Thursday I see my friends. Do you want to come?

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: أكيد. تصبح على خير، منشوفك بكرا.
dialogue.english: Sure. Good night, see you tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: وإنتي من أهله.
dialogue.english: And you (too).
